analysis.investment_thesis: Aptus Value Housing Finance is a mortgage lender and must be excluded from Magic Formula ROIC/earnings-yield ranking, but of the five names here it presents the most interesting qualitative case: P/E of 13.9x (forward 11.2x) against a 45.7% net profit CAGR over 8 years, focused on an underserved rural/semi-urban affordable housing niche with ROE of 18.6%. The valuation is the most reasonable in the group, but it is a financial company operating at 1.57x leverage, not a Magic Formula candidate.
key_strengths: Outstanding earnings compounding: net profit grew at 45.7% CAGR over 8 years from INR 37 Cr (2017) to INR 751 Cr (2025), with no year of decline
Niche positioning in rural/semi-urban affordable housing creates a relatively low-competition, high-stickiness borrower base with strong demand tailwinds from India's housing shortage
Reasonable leverage for an HFC at D/E 1.57x, with strong institutional ownership — FII 30.3% + DII 29.4% = 59.8% institutional confidence
key_risks: OCF is negative every single year (0/5) as is structurally normal for a lending business, but growth is entirely dependent on continued access to wholesale funding at acceptable rates
Promoter holding of only 23.86% is low for a financial institution — corporate governance and strategic continuity risks are higher than peers
Rising interest rate environment compresses net interest margins; finance costs grew at 40.3% CAGR, tracking loan book growth but squeezing spreads if cost of funds rises
red_flags: Financial company: Magic Formula cannot be applied — operating CF is structurally negative and EBIT/EV is not a meaningful measure for an HFC
Promoter stake of 23.86% is below comfort threshold for a financial company where management alignment is critical
Loan book growing at ~25–30% annually into a rural borrower base carries credit cycle risk that is not yet visible in reported NPAs
analysis.detailed_analysis: As a housing finance company, Aptus is excluded from the Magic Formula — negative OCF is structural (loan disbursements flow through operating activities), and leverage is business-model-inherent, not a signal of poor capital discipline. Setting the formula aside, Aptus is the best-valued of the five stocks presented: P/E of 13.9x with a long-duration 45.7% profit CAGR is a combination that rarely exists in Indian financial services. The rural/semi-urban affordable housing segment benefits from strong government tailwind (PMAY, priority-sector lending) and limited competition from large private banks. I would want to understand NPA trends and funding cost trajectory before getting more constructive, but at P/E 13.9x it at least deserves to be in a watch list rather than immediately discarded.
